standard_prerequisites.name: m-covered family
standard_prerequisites.statement: The family is contained in the union of m cosets, each prescribing one image of a permutation.

standard_prerequisites.name: Certificate of a member
standard_prerequisites.statement: A set of images prescribed for that member; the size bound is the conclusion.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what the statement bounds.

standard_prerequisites.name: Degree reduction
standard_prerequisites.statement: Reducing a function by fixing the coordinates of a coset gives a function of lower degree on the remaining coordinates.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the tool that lets the degree-one classification be applied.

core_obligations: Use the covering hypothesis to write the family as a union of cosets and fix one of them (source line 586).
Reduce the function along the fixed coset so that the degree-one classification becomes applicable, and obtain a small certificate for the reduced function (source lines 587-601).
Lift that certificate back to the original family, which yields the certificate of size m plus one (source line 601).

proof_roadmap.step: Fix a coset and reduce the degree.
Apply the degree-one classification after the reduction.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 581-585: if the family is covered by m cosets and the characteristic function has degree at most one after the restriction forced by that covering, then every member has a certificate of the form given by the m prescribed images together with one more image, so the common certificate size is at most m plus one. The proof (source lines 586-602) is a reduction argument that the statement does not display: fixing the coset restricts the function to the remaining coordinates, the degree-one classification applies to that restriction, and the resulting small certificate has to be lifted back through the covering to produce the certificate named in the statement. The statement records only the size bound.
